title.narrative: Second Solomon Islands Roads and Aviation Project

description.narrative: SIRAP2 was approved by the Board on June 1, 2022, with US$89.21 million financing. The project aims to improve the climate resilience and safety of the Recipient's road and aviation sectors through four components: (i) Climate Resilience and Safety Investments in the Aviation Sector, (ii) Climate Resilience and Safety Investments in the Road Sector, (iii) Institutional Strengthening and Project Management, and (iv) Contingent Emergency Response. The proposed SIRAP2 AF is for scale-up investments in Suavanao Airfield, ground support equipment at Honiara and Munda Airports, rehabilitation and improvements to Malaita Roads, Technical Assistance for road and aviation sectors, and implementation support, as well as cost overruns for existing SIRAP2 activities.Component 1: Climate Resilience and Safety Investments in the Aviation Sector finances the following activities: (a) Subcomponent 1.1: Honiara Airport Infrastructure Investments, which finances overlay of the existing asphalt paved runway and installation of airfield ground lighting; supply and replacement of perimeter fence; design and construction of a rescue fire service vehicle station; design and construction of an air traffic control tower; design and construction of a new aviation complex building; installation of an automatic weather observation station; provision of crash alarms; provision of standby generators; and equipment support. This subcomponent will also finance additional equipment support under the proposed AF and commissioning of CRV through a restructuring, which is being processed with the proposed AF.(b) Subcomponent 1.2: Munda Airport Infrastructure Investments, which finances (i) the design and construction of an air traffic control tower, and (ii) provision of crash alarms. This subcomponent will also finance additional equipment support under the proposed AF.(c) Subcomponent 1.3: Santa Cruz Airfield Infrastructure Investments, which finances runway pavement works at Santa Cruz (Lata) Airfield in Temotu Province.(d) Subcomponent 1.4: Modernization of Air Navigation Systems which will finance (i) Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) grand stations, and (ii) alternative energy source to be provided in Makira-Ulawa and Temotu Provinces.(e) Subcomponent 1.5: Regional Airport Maintenance to maintain critical mechanical and electrical assets.(f) Subcomponent 1.6: Suavanao Airfield Infrastructure Investments (new subcomponent), which will finance runway pavement works at Suavanao Airfield in Isabel Province under the proposed AF.Activities under Component 1 are located on Guadalcanal Island (Honiara Airport), New Georgia Island (Munda Airport), Makira-Ulawa Province, Temotu Province (Santa Cruz Airfield), and Isabel Province (Suavanao Airfield).Component 2: Climate Resilience and Safety Investments in the Road Sector finances the following activities with climate resilience and road safety improvements:(a) Subcomponent 2.1: Malaita Bridges Improvement, which finances the replacement of four bridges—Kolofe1 and Kolofe2 Bridges on North Road, and Su’u Harbor and Bira Bridges on South Road. (b) Subcomponent 2.2: Noro Roads Improvement, which finances climate resilience and safety improvements to 10 km of Noro Roads in Western Province.(c) Subcomponent 2.3: Malaita Roads Improvement (new subcomponent), which will finance (i) routine maintenance and regravelling (including upgrading key vulnerable spots to enhance climate resilience and improving road safety) on 21 km of East Road between Baratoro and Atori, and (ii) sealing about 12 km of the gravel road between Auki Gwaunaru’u Airfield Junction and Kwaisuliniu Road Junction on North Road under the proposed AF.Activities under Component 2 are located on Malaita Island (Malaita Bridges and Roads), and New Georgia Island (Noro Roads). Component 3: Institutional Strengthening and Project Management finances the following activities:(a) Subcomponent 3.1. Technical Assistance activities include: (i) a consulting service for design and supervision of building and civil works under Subcomponents 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, and Component 2; (ii) preparation of a national airports development plan; (iii) technical support and training to MCA and Solomon Airlines; (iv) climate resilient road asset management improvement; (v) road safety audits; (vi) road safety capacity improvement, and (vii) activities to address the identified gender gap within MCA and expansion of the GBV training and awareness raising activities. This subcomponent will also finance additional design and supervision consultancy for the scale-up activities under Subcomponents 1.6 and 2.3, for additional technical assistance to Solomon Airlines, training, and for new technical support and training to CAASI and SIACL under the proposed AF.(b) Subcomponent 3.2. Project Implementation Support include PST contracted staff and operating costs associated with implementation of the project, and yearly audits of the project accounts that SIG will submit to the World Bank. This subcomponent will also finance additional project implementation support under the proposed AF.Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response. This zero-dollar component is designed to provide swift response in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, by enabling SIG to request the World Bank to reallocate project funds to support emergency response and reconstruction. The proposed AF will fully be funded by IDA, with an estimated total cost of $51.20 million, and no other donor investments are envisaged.
To improve the climate resilience and safety of the Recipient's road and aviation sectors, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

condition.narrative: In order to carry out Part 1(e) of the Project, the Recipient shall enter into a Performance-Based Contract, with a private sectorcontractor selected on the basis of terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association, inaccordancewith the provisions included or referred to in this Agreement (“PBC Contractor”), under terms and conditions acceptableto the Association. (Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall carry out, jointly with the Association, not later than three years after the Effective Date, or such otherperiod as may be agreed with the Association, a mid-term review of the Project to assess the status of Project implementation, asmeasured against the Project indicators acceptable to the Association, and compliance with the legal covenants. (Section II.2 ofSchedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall furnish to the Association each Project Report not later than forty-five (45) days after the end of eachcalendar quarter, covering the calendar quarter. (Section II.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation, the Project Support Team within the Ministry of Communication andAviation, with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall: (a) be responsible for, interalia, day to day implementation of the Project including contract management, procurement, financial management, preparing and/orconsolidating Annual Work Plans and Budgets, technical aspects, environmental and social risks management, monitoring, reporting,and evaluation; (b) report to the focal point within the Ministry of Communication and Aviation and the focal point within theMinistry of Infrastructure Development; and (c) be comprised of, inter alia: (i) a project manager; (ii) a deputy project manager;(iii) a national safeguards officer; (iv) a community liaison officer; (v) a Project accountant; (vi) a procurement specialist;(vii) an administrative assistant; and (viii) a finance manager. (Section I.A.2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association, by not later than November 30 of each year during the implementation ofthe Project, an Annual Work Plan and Budget for the Project. The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented inaccordance with the Annual Work Plans and Budgets approved by the Association for the respective fiscal year. (Sections I.D.1 andI.D.2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall: (a) by not later than three months after the Effective Date, prepare and adopt a Project Operations Manual;and (b) thereafter ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Project Operations Manual. (Section C.3 ofSchedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

To ensure proper oversight of the Project at the national level, the Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation,the National Steering Committee, with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall be: (a)responsible for, inter alia, providing Project oversight, approving Annual Work Plans and Budgets, and advising on Project relatedmatters; and (b) comprised of, inter alia: (i) Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance and Treasury (or his or herdesignee); (ii) the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Infrastructure Development (or his or her designee); (iii) the PermanentSecretary of the Ministry of Communication and Aviation (or his or her designee); (iv) the Provincial Secretary of Malaita Province(or his or her designee); (v) the Provincial Secretary of Western Province (or his or her designee); (vi) the Provincial Secretaryof Temotu Province (or his or her designee); and (vii) the Deputy Secretary – Technical of the Ministry of InfrastructureDevelopment (or his or her designee). (Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)
